`mesh_set_custom_aabb` call should be needed only within the `else` block above.

For `needs_clear == true` case `mesh_add_surface` call updates `mesh->aabb` accordingly:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e82870e250a326c94e03d658306db94e1b116c2d/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/mesh_storage.cpp#L489-L493

Also when `has_bones == true` then `needs_clear == true`, so the check is redundant, this would be sufficient (within the `else` block):
```
RS::get_singleton()->mesh_set_custom_aabb(mesh, sd.aabb);
```

+The code is self explaining, the 2-line comment is really not needed.

I think youre right that `has_bones` is only true on the `needs_clear` path so the ternary was redundant so I've move the call into the branches.

I think there is an issue with setting it only in the `else` block though `mesh_clear()` resets `mesh->aabb` but not `custom_aabb` (`mesh_storage.cpp#L884`). So if the fast path sets a custom AABB and a later draw hits `needs_clear` with different bounds, for example because the vertex count changes, `mesh_add_surface()` updates `mesh->aabb` correctly but the stale `custom_aabb` still shadows it in `mesh_get_aabb()`. The polygon then gets culled against the old bounds.

I reproduced it by 

* drawing a square
* moving it off-screen with the same vertex count so the fast path sets `custom_aabb`
* replacing it with a 5-vertex polygon at the center so it takes the `needs_clear` path

so I set the custom AABB on the fast path and clear it on needs_clear which falls back to the surface AABB.

The polygon then gets culled against the old bounds.

Ah, you're right, I've overlooked this.

Ideally after updating vertex buffer data we would be updating `RendererRD::MeshStorage::Mesh::Surface::aabb` instead of setting `RendererRD::MeshStorage::Mesh::Surface::custom_aabb`, in such case clearing the manually set aabb in the `if (needs_clear)` branch would be not needed like I've suggested.
But there's no `mesh_set_custom_aabb` counterpart for updating `aabb` specifically, so either such method would need to be added, or we need to utilize the `custom_aabb`. And using `custom_aabb` should be fine, it is already being used e.g. in `Sprite3D` in a similar scenario:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/dff2b9bb66a01d8c1a207531b0752405c7399124/scene/3d/sprite_3d.cpp#L279-L282
